idiom_name: test fixture implements the collaborator interface and passes this (std::function/lambda for one-method seams)
implementation_notes: The GoogleTest/Catch2 fixture is already a class, so the classic Self Shunt needs no new type: derive the fixture from the collaborator's abstract interface, override the callback to record into fixture members, and hand the SUT this through its constructor, setter or registration call. For a seam whose contract is already a std::function or a template parameter, a lambda capturing fixture or local state replaces the whole-class shunt and keeps the double inside one test body -- strictly speaking Meszaros' Inner Test Double -- so the language note is that the lighter local form wins for one-callback seams. Keep the whole-class form when the SUT asks for an abstract base class with virtual functions that a lambda cannot satisfy, or when several tests in the fixture observe the same callback.
pitfalls: The SUT must not keep the reference past the test: storing this in a longer-lived object leaves a dangling pointer once the fixture is destroyed, and the framework destroys the fixture after each test.

The fixture inherits from both the test base class and the collaborator interface, so member-name or destructor clashes become compile errors; the interface's unused methods must still be implemented.
A lambda that captures local state by reference is safe only while it is consumed inside the test body; storing it in a member or passing it to something that keeps the std::function dangles.
